title: How many pieces does the folded rope give?
description: A straight rope cut once gives two pieces, and folded once and cut gives three. The pattern gives twelve pieces for ten folds and r plus two pieces for r folds.
teaching_notes: One idea: each extra fold adds one more piece, so the pieces are the folds plus two. Watch for students who say ten folds give ten pieces.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the matchstick steps: the same addition happens at every step, so the count is the start plus the number of steps.
video_script.substitution: The method of the matchstick steps, where the same two matchsticks are added at every step, with one more piece added at every fold.
video_script.anchor: a straight rope that is folded and then cut
video_script.payoff_line: Ten folds give twelve pieces, and r folds give r plus two pieces

final_answer.value: 12 pieces for 10 folds, and r + 2 pieces for r folds
final_answer.spoken: twelve pieces for ten folds, and r plus two pieces for r folds

hold_back: Answer: 12 pieces for 10 folds, and r + 2 pieces for r folds
never_show: the finished formula before the answer beat
maths_rules: no fold and one cut: 2 pieces; one fold and a cut: 3 pieces
each extra fold adds one more piece, so pieces = folds + 2
check r = 0: 2 pieces; r = 1: 3 pieces, both match the picture
video_script.design: One idea: every extra fold adds one more layer under the cut, so one more piece. Assumes the example of the same addition at every step. The rope and the cut stay on the stage.
open_questions: The picture is not in the extracted book text. The book's r plus 2 fits a rope folded back and forth in a zigzag, with the cut through every layer; halving folds would give a different pattern.
